1-101. E sta b lish m en t o f  B oard. There is established, effective October 1,1982,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any commuter authority providing  
commuter rail service. The Board shall perform its functions subject to the  
availability of funds.

1-102. P u b lic H ea rin g. The board shall conduct a public hearing on the dispute  
at which each party shall appear and provide testimony.

1-103. In itia l R eport. The board shall report on the dispute within 30 days 
after the date of its creation.

1-104. F in a l O ffers. If the parties have not settled the dispute within ten days  
after the board’s report, the board shall require the parties to submit, within  
five days, their final offers for settlement of the dispute.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12384 (47 FR 43935, Federal Register of October 5, 1982; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and the Delaware Transportation Authority, and Certain Labor Organizations and signed October 1, 1982. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and the Delaware Transportation Authority and certain labor organizations. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 1 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (whole). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12384 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; they are not recorded as later events because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence, so the claim states the functional spending without a date. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
